On this page

File standard ​

The file standard defines what a Mosaic file is: its index, sections, nodes and component references. This page describes the schema. The format, by example walks through a real archive.

standard/ holds two documents. Both are generated, so they are never edited by hand:

FileDescribesGenerated from
mosaic-index-file.schema.jsonThe index of a Mosaic file (JSON Schema 2020-12)src/mosaic-json-file.tsp
mosaic-api.openapi3.jsonThe HTTP API for keeping tesserae and their versions (OpenAPI 3)src/mosaic-api.tsp

They are checked in so consumers can use them without running the toolchain.

Generating them ​

The source of truth is TypeSpec in src/. To change the standard, edit the .tsp and regenerate:

bash
cd src
npm install
npm run compile-json-spec    # mosaic-json-file.tsp -> standard/mosaic-index-file.schema.json
npm run compile-api-spec     # mosaic-api.tsp       -> standard/mosaic-api.openapi3.json

Commit the regenerated output alongside the spec change. Two more scripts carry the change into the reference implementation:

bash
npm run gen-sdk-index-ts     # index schema -> sdk/ts/src/MosaicIndexFile.ts
npm run gen-api-sdk          # OpenAPI      -> sdk/ts/src/api/ (types, routes, client)

Every object schema is sealed ("additionalProperties": false). A property the standard does not name is invalid, not ignored, and code generators produce exact types with no catch-all field.

The index file ​

MosaicIndexFile is the root. A file is valid when its index validates against this schema.

ts
model MosaicIndexFile {
    header: MosaicFileHeader;              // { MosaicVersion: string }
    "imports": ImportNode[];               // { uri: string; integrity?: string }
    componentTables: ComponentTableReference[];
    sections: MosaicDataSection[];
}

model MosaicDataSection {
    header: MosaicProvenanceHeader;
    nodes: MosaicNode[];
}

model MosaicNode {
    id: uuid;
    components?: ComponentReference[];
}

model ComponentReference {
    type: string;                          // e.g. "khronos::gltf::meshPrimitive"
    id: string;                            // names this reference within the node
    index?: int32 = -1;                    // row in the type's table; -1 = no value
    operation?: OperationType = OperationType.VALUE;
}

enum OperationType { PASS_THROUGH, DELETE, VALUE }
json
{
  "header": { "MosaicVersion": "post-alpha" },
  "imports": [],
  "componentTables": [],
  "sections": [{
    "header": {
      "id": "hello",
      "message": "A single named node",
      "dataVersion": "1.0.0",
      "author": "ada@example.com",
      "timestamp": "2026-11-08T12:00:00Z",
      "application": "by hand"
    },
    "nodes": [{
      "id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
      "components": [{ "type": "core::name", "id": "Hello" }]
    }]
  }]
}
ModelFieldsNotes
MosaicFileHeaderMosaicVersionWhich version of the standard the file follows
ImportNodeuri, integrity?Another Mosaic file, optionally pinned by a hash
ComponentTableReferencefilename, type, schemaOne table of component values. type is NDJSON or PARQUET, and schema is the JSON Schema of its rows, inlined
MosaicDataSectionheader, nodesOne layer of edits
MosaicProvenanceHeaderid, message, dataVersion, author, timestamp, applicationWho made the layer, when and why. All required
MosaicNodeid (uuid), components?A node is an id and its references
ComponentReferencetype, id, index?, operation?See The format

What the schemas say, and what they don't ​

The schemas fix the shape of a file. A few rules sit in the description of the format rather than in the schema itself:

  • Sections are ordered. A later section wins over an earlier one, and operation says how: VALUE sets, DELETE unsets, PASS_THROUGH leaves the earlier value alone.
  • index: -1 means no value. The reference's id is the whole of what it says. This is how value-less components work.
  • Imports layer underneath. An imported file's sections count as older than the importing file's own.

Some things are not standardised yet and are defined only by what the reference implementation does:

  • The archive container. A .tsr is a zip with index.json at its root and one <type>.ndjson per component table. No schema describes the zip itself.
  • Component schemas. The standard says a table carries a schema but not which component types exist. core::*, khronos::gltf::*, w3c::svg and ifc4::* are all defined in the SDK (see below), as is the x-mosaic-id keyword that names a schema's type.
  • Composition. Inheritance through core::inherit, hierarchy through core::child, and the mapping to glTF are SDK behaviour.

Component schemas ​

Component schemas are ordinary JSON Schema documents with an x-mosaic-id naming the type they describe. They live with the code that understands them, not in standard/:

NamespaceSchemasLocation
core::name, child, inherit, transform, edgessdk/ts/src/core/schemas/
khronos::gltf::buffer, bufferView, accessor, meshPrimitive, material, image, sampler, texturesdk/ts/src/gltf/schemas/
w3c::svgsdk/ts/src/svg/schemas/
ifc4::entity, propertySet, quantitySet, units, rel::*sdk/ifc4/src/schemas/

Anyone can define more, such as acme::geometry::wall. Since each archive inlines the schema of every table it carries, a reader can validate a component type it has never seen before. mosaic codegen turns component schemas into typed classes (see Code generation).

The second document in standard/, mosaic-api.openapi3.json, is described in API standard.
